metadata.title: Where Seniors Now Outnumber Kids
metadata.section: Section D: Demographics, Real Estate & Urban Drift
metadata.data_notes: National shares from the yearly ACS. County counts use 5-year ACS averages, so each point covers the 5 years ending that year.

events.label: About 860 counties have more seniors than kids

explanation.summary: America is getting older. The share of people aged 65 and over is rising while the share of children is falling. In a growing number of counties there are now more seniors than kids.
explanation.methodology: National shares of people under 18 and 65 and over from the Census Bureau's American Community Survey (table B01001), 1-year estimates. County counts compare the same two age groups in every US county using 5-year ACS estimates, so each point covers the five years ending that year.

key_findings.title: 2011: The First Boomers Turn 65
key_findings.description: Seniors were 13.2% of the population and children 23.8%. About 320 counties had more seniors than children.
key_findings.significance: The start of a long, predictable aging wave.

key_findings.title: 2019: Counties Tip Over
key_findings.description: The number of counties with more seniors than kids had nearly tripled since 2009, to about 860.
key_findings.significance: Rural counties age first, as young people move to cities.

key_findings.title: 2024: 1,266 Counties
key_findings.description: Seniors are now 18.0% of Americans and children 21.4%. In 1,266 counties, about 40% of all US counties, seniors outnumber children.
key_findings.significance: This changes demand for schools, hospitals and workers.
